summary: THIRD_PARTY.md generated by tools/build-third-party.mjs from package-lock.json, cargo metadata for the shipped Windows target, Lich, Godot, fonts and every admitted shared-asset sourceLicense

coordination.notes: Same generated-doc shape as tools/build-player-data-doc.mjs (F6's sibling in this lane) and tools/build-crossing-build-list.mjs before it: prose in the generator, figures derived on every run, floors that refuse to publish from a broken read. Registered as test:third-party in both package.json and tools/test-suites.json, which is why the latter joins the touches list.

findings.what: The npm source is package-lock.json, not node_modules/<dep>/package.json
findings.judgement: The increment names the latter. The lockfile carries both the resolved version and the licence for every package, is committed, and is identical on every machine; node_modules is absent in a fresh worktree and is a junction to another checkout in this one. Reading it would make the document's contents depend on who ran the generator, which is the drift the generator exists to prevent.

findings.what: cargo metadata is filtered to x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
findings.judgement: src-tauri/Cargo.lock lists 469 packages, every platform's. Only 319 survive the Windows cfg and reach the binary anybody installs. An unfiltered list would name GTK and Android crates this app has never shipped, and would also differ between a Windows dev machine and a Linux CI runner, so the filter is what makes the document both true and reproducible.

findings.what: Lich's BSD-3-Clause is verified against a local install, not asserted
findings.judgement: docs/ENGINE.md says verify rather than trust. C:/Ruby4Lich5/Lich5/LICENSE read: 'BSD 3-Clause License', with 'Copyright (c) 2005-2006, Murray Miron', 'Copyright (c) 2006-2020, Matt Lowe (Tillmen)' and 'Copyright (c) 2021-present, Elanthia Online'. The verification is a run-time check, never document content: a document whose text depended on whether the machine had Lich would drift between machines by design. On a machine without Lich the run prints NOT CHECKED naming the paths it looked at.

Checked rather than assumed: git ls-files finds no .ttf/.otf/.woff/.woff2 anywhere in the tree, and src/index.css asks for 'Segoe UI' then the system stack. So no font file is redistributed and no font licence applies. Recorded in the document, because 'fonts' is on the increment's list and an absent section would read as an oversight.
